newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs to start bourse trade on June 12.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs to start bourse trade on June 12.

text.p: The 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation programme will start trade on the Warsaw bourse's main market on June 12, the bourse's president said on Wednesday.

"The bourse's board has taken the decision to introduce all the shares of the 15 National Investment Funds to bourse trade and has designated the date of June 12 as the date of first listing," Wieslaw Rozlucki told a news conference.
He added that the funds had to submit audited 1996 reports by June 10 for the June 12 date to stand.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme are entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund.
The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
On Wednesday the National Securities Depository (KDPW) said 3,372 of the units had been converted into shares.
The 15 NFIs were given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.
